caption: A demolition hammer chips a concrete floor, and an occasional spark flicks where the bit strikes embedded stone.

sa.check: A demolition hammer with its bit on a concrete floor.
The hammer chips the floor: the bit strikes repeatedly and pieces break off.
A spark flicks where the bit strikes embedded stone.
Sparks come only at some blows, not every one.
The strike comes first and the spark follows.

pc.expect: Sparks appear only at the moment of a blow, at the point where the bit meets the floor, and each is gone at once; between blows nothing glows.
pc.fail: A spark stays lit on the floor after the bit lifts; or sparks appear while the hammer is held off the floor; or the bit glows steadily; or sparks appear at a point away from the bit.

pc.expect: One hammer with one bit; chips that break off are pieces of the floor and stay on the floor; sparks leave nothing behind.
pc.fail: Glowing dots stay on the floor after a blow; or chips vanish in mid-air; or the bit duplicates or vanishes; or chips appear from nowhere away from the bit.

pc.expect: Chips and any spark fragments fly out from the bit and fall to the floor, going dark within a short distance.
pc.fail: Chips or sparks rise and hang in the air; or climb steadily; or sparks lie glowing on the floor for the rest of the clip.

pc.expect: The concrete breaks into hard chips and leaves a pitted hole; the bit stays a rigid steel point.
pc.fail: The concrete dents like clay and springs back; or the floor ripples like water; or the bit bends or curls; or the hole closes up between blows.

pc.expect: The bit strikes the floor's surface and enters only as far as the hole it makes; the hammer keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The bit passes deep through the floor as if through air; or the hammer sinks into the floor; or the hammer changes shape; or the floor turns transparent.

pc.expect: The hammer's colour and the floor's surface away from the hole stay the same.
pc.fail: The hammer changes colour; or the floor changes texture away from the hole; or the surroundings rearrange.

note: Who holds the hammer is not judged.
